name: Sophora alopecuroides seed
short: Two 8-day placebo-controlled trials of a seed extract by mouth (50 took it in each, in opioid withdrawal): no side effects; liver, kidney, blood tests not significantly affected. Longer use unknown.
text: The only human safety data found come from two placebo-controlled trials of a seed extract of Sophora alopecuroides var. alopecuroides, each in 100 abstinent people with opioid dependence (50 extract, 50 placebo), with three 400 mg capsules taken once a day by mouth for 8 days. In people who had used opium, the extract did not significantly change liver enzymes, bilirubin, kidney tests, blood counts or prothrombin (clotting) time compared with placebo, and there was no adverse drug effect; the extract's main alkaloids were sophocarpine, matrine and sophoramine. In people who had used heroin, no side effect was noted and the extract had no significant effect on liver and kidney function or blood counts. Because both trials lasted 8 days, the abstracts give no information on longer use. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
